newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch carriers reschedule to beat night ban.
newsitem.headline: Dutch carriers reschedule to beat night ban.

text.p: Dutch carriers Martinair and KLM Royal Dutch Airlines have been forced to reschedule certain flights as a result of the night take-off ban on noisier aircraft at Schiphol which comes into force on Tuesday.

The ban, which was only confirmed on Monday, will prevent aircraft such as the DC-10 and the Boeing in the 747-100, 200, 300 and SP versions, from taking off between 2300 and 0600 local (2100-0400 GMT), in a bid to cut noise levels at the airport.
Gerard Draai, spokesman for Martinair, said this ban particularly affects its Boeing 747-200 freighter departure to Taipei which is scheduled to leave at 2100 local (1900 GMT) on Friday night.

This flight has been departing at 0200-0300 local (0000-0100 GMT) over the past few weeks. Under the new rules, it will have to postpone take-off until after 0600 local (0400 GMT) resulting in further delays.
"We still have not got any clear information from the airport," Draai told Reuters. The next step for the carrier was to talk to its lawyers, he added.
KLM Cargo is also affected since U.S. carrier Atlas Air operates 747-200s on KLM's behalf. A KLM Cargo spokesman said three flights a week are hit by the ban.

One such flight, which departs on Saturdays to Dubai and Kuala Lumpur, has been rescheduled. It used to depart at 0530 local (0330 GMT) but will now leave at 0640 local (0440 GMT) as there was some flexibility in its landing slot at Dubai.
The airline is in talks with the airport authority over the other two departures, which are to Dubai and Chicago.

"We do share the view that measures are needed to avoid excess noise at Schiphol but KLM believes it can be achieved through slot allocation measures. But there needs to be careful preparation and it is not realistic to put the plans into action before the summer schedule of 1998," the KLM official said.
The Dutch government said on Monday that the measures being introduced on Tuesday are insufficient and has given Schiphol airport until September 1 to come up with tougher action.
If not, the government will said it would consider closing all or part of the airport. -- Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
